source.checked: All 16 candidate IDs exist and are not obsolete; definitions and six overlap clusters inspected against the unmodified release. No ontology content repackaged.

recommendations.rationale: Broaden the definition to include known subtypes. The parent concept does not mean subtype unknown.

previousValues.definition: Blood in the urine, without specifying microscopic or visible haematuria.
previousValues.help: Blood in the urine, without specifying microscopic or visible haematuria.

proposedValues.definition: Documented blood in the urine, including microscopic or visible haematuria; the subtype may be known or unknown.
proposedValues.help: Includes microscopic and visible haematuria. Record the subtype separately when known. A missing urine result is unknown, not absent.

recommendations.rationale: Retain documented microscopic haematuria. Do not treat unspecified haematuria as sufficient evidence or introduce a new RBC threshold.
Retain visible haematuria. Record the historical event; no inference of persistence or cause.
Correct overly narrow unspecified-type definition. Known sensorineural impairment also falls within the broad concept.

previousValues.definition: Documented hearing impairment of unspecified type.
previousValues.help: Documented hearing impairment of unspecified type.

proposedValues.definition: Documented reduction in hearing, whether or not the type or laterality is known.
proposedValues.help: Includes hearing impairment with a known or unknown type. Record sensorineural type and laterality separately when documented.

recommendations.rationale: Retain explicit hearing-assessment evidence; subjective hearing difficulty cannot establish the type.
Retain explicit documentation that both ears are affected; preserve laterality.
Clarify one-or-more wording so multiple cysts do not appear excluded by a singular question.

previousValues.question: Has a renal cyst been documented on imaging?
previousValues.definition: A documented renal cyst without a number or distribution requirement.
previousValues.help: A documented renal cyst without a number or distribution requirement.

proposedValues.question: Has at least one renal cyst been documented on imaging?
proposedValues.definition: One or more documented renal cysts; number, distribution and morphology require separate detail.
proposedValues.help: Includes a single cyst or multiple cysts. This finding alone does not establish cystic dysplasia or inherited cystic disease.

recommendations.rationale: Retain report-based multiple-cyst finding. The ontology does not supply a numerical cutoff to implement here.
Retain documented CKD history. Automated chronicity assessment requires a separate dated rule.
Retain as broad context/fallback when this is what the record supports; do not make it an independent disease-discriminating score or require it to be answered again after CKD.
Retain documented hypertension. A single elevated blood pressure is not equivalent to the HPO chronic-pressure concept.
Retain explicit documented stage. Do not require dialysis or infer this stage from any dialysis exposure.
Retain clinician-documented impaired coordination; unqualified dizziness or imbalance is insufficient.
Retain documented reduced muscle tone; weakness is a different finding.
Add age at the historical assessment. The source definition restricts this term to children younger than five.

previousValues.question: Has global developmental delay been documented?

proposedValues.question: Was global developmental delay documented in early childhood, before age five?
proposedValues.definition: A documented history of global developmental delay in a child younger than five at the relevant assessment.
proposedValues.help: An older patient can have a documented childhood history. Do not use a new assessment of adult difficulties or an isolated developmental concern to establish this finding. If the childhood timing cannot be established, record unknown.

recommendations.rationale: Retain explicit documented tumour diagnosis. An unspecified renal mass is insufficient; preserve diagnosis date for later research use.
